ev.q: During the COVID-19 pandemic, age-adjusted stroke mortality rates increased among both Black and White adults
During 2020–2021, an estimated 3,835 excess stroke deaths occurred among Black adults (9.4% more than expected)
The absolute difference in AASDR between Black and White adults increased 21.7% (from 31.3 to 38.0)
Analyses were stratified by sex and age group (35–64, 65–84, and ≥85 years).
Compared with that during the prepandemic period, the absolute difference in AASDR between Black and White adults during the pandemic was 21.7% higher
Analysts used National Vital Statistics System (NVSS) mortality data accessed via CDC WONDER

methods_quotes.q: Nonoverlapping 95% CIs for rates, absolute differences, or relative differences between two periods or two groups (e.g., women versus men) were considered statistically significant.
Analyses were stratified by sex and age group (35–64, 65–84, and ≥85 years).
expected rates for 2020 and 2021 were calculated, assuming the APC during 2015–2019 would continue during 2020–2021
The relative difference was measured by rate ratios calculated as AASDR among Black adults divided by AASDR among White adults.
95% CIs are estimated by the Monte Carlo simulation–based approach by sampling 5,000 normal distributions based on the AASDRs and SEs
For AASDRs, 95% CIs are calculated using Anderson-Rosenberg methods with the normal approximations of the 95% CIs
